description: We are TapaTrío, a multidisciplinary team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Guadalajara, Mexico. Our goal is to develop innovative health monitoring software for astronauts during space missions. We aim to combine biomedical technology, artificial intelligence, data analysis, and software development to create practical solutions that improve astronaut health, safety, and mission success.
summary:
During deep-space missions to the Moon and Mars, communication delays of up to 44 minutes render real-time Earth-based telemedicine impossible during sudden, life-threatening cardiac emergencies. AEGIS (Autonomous Environmental & General-health Integrated System) is an offline-first, autonomous medical monitoring software engineered to detect, classify, and guide immediate crew intervention for Ventricular Fibrillation (VF) and acute arrhythmias in microgravity. 

Built on a deterministic hybrid architecture that integrates real-time ECG signal processing, a Finite State Machine (FSM), and a JSON-driven Rule-Based System, AEGIS eliminates black-box AI unpredictability in human-rated medical software. By combining continuous physiological telemetry with step-by-step Just-in-Time (JITT) clinical guidance, AEGIS empowers non-physician astronauts to execute life-saving cardiac protocols autonomously when seconds determine survival.
details:
AEGIS (Autonomous Environmental & General-health Integrated System) is an offline-first, autonomous medical monitoring and clinical decision-support console engineered for long-duration spaceflight. Focusing on Ventricular Fibrillation (VF) and acute cardiac arrhythmias—among the highest-mortality emergencies in NASA’s list of 119 spaceflight medical conditions—AEGIS enables non-physician astronauts to detect, verify, and treat life-threatening cardiac events without waiting up to 44 minutes for ground control guidance.

To guarantee clinical auditability and zero-latency execution, AEGIS operates on a four-layer Deterministic Hybrid Architecture:

  1. Signal Processing Layer (Real-Time ECG & Cabin Telemetry): Continuously ingests simulated or sensor-streamed ECG waveforms alongside spacecraft environmental data (cabin $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{O}_2$, and radiation). It applies digital filtering, QRS complex detection, R-R interval regularity checks, and frequency-domain spectral analysis to distinguish normal microgravity cardiac adaptation from ventricular tachycardia or chaotic Ventricular Fibrillation waveforms, while cross-correlating environmental triggers (such as hypercapnia).
  2. JSON Configuration & Knowledge Layer: Decouples medical domain knowledge from application logic. A declarative JSON schema defines all monitored variables, microgravity-calibrated baseline thresholds (per NASA-STD-3001), clinical evaluation rules, Finite State Machine (FSM) states, and explicit transition conditions. Flight surgeons can audit, update, or expand the knowledge base to cover additional NASA medical conditions without modifying core engine code.
    • Rule-Based System: Evaluates extracted signal features and multi-day longitudinal trends against the JSON clinical ruleset to produce transparent, verifiable risk predicates.
    • Finite State Machine (FSM): Governs each astronaut’s clinical lifecycle through strict, deterministic states (NOMINAL, PRE_ARRHYTHMIC_CAUTION, VF_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED, CRITICAL_VF_EMERGENCY, and POST_RESUSCITATION_RECOVERY), preventing erratic alert flickering and guaranteeing predictable, reproducible transitions.
  3. Autonomous Crew Console & Just-in-Time (JITT) Interface: Provides a multi-crew command dock running simultaneous active sessions for a 5-person crew, an interactive anatomical body map, longitudinal vital sign charts compared against pre-flight baselines, automated onboard medkit/AED inventory tracking, and step-by-step visual emergency protocols.

Benefits of AEGIS

  • Earth-Independent Survival: Eliminates the deep-space communication latency bottleneck during sudden cardiac arrest, where intervention within minutes is critical for survival.
  • Aerospace-Grade Determinism: Unlike black-box machine learning models that can behave unpredictably on edge cases, pairing digital signal processing with an FSM and Rule-Based System ensures 100% deterministic, explainable, and human-ratable medical logic.
  • Reduced Cognitive Load Under Stress: Translates complex ECG waveform anomalies into clear color-coded alerts and guided Just-in-Time (JITT) checklists tailored for crew members without specialized cardiology training.
  • Environment-Aware Diagnostics: Correlates closed-cabin hazards ($\text{CO}_2$ buildup or radiation spikes) with cardiac telemetry to identify environmental root causes before administering medication.

Intended Impact

AEGIS is designed to bridge the operational gap between ground-assisted telemedicine in Low Earth Orbit (ISS) and full medical autonomy required for NASA’s Artemis lunar bases and crewed Mars missions. Beyond protecting astronauts during deep-space exploration, its modular JSON knowledge architecture can scale across all 119 NASA spaceflight medical conditions. Furthermore, the system has direct terrestrial applications in extreme, disconnected environments—such as submarines, polar research stations, offshore platforms, and remote rural clinics—where non-specialists must manage acute cardiac emergencies without immediate physician access.

How Our Project Is Creative

  • Deterministic Hybrid Architecture Over Black-Box AI: Rather than relying on opaque neural networks for life-critical triage, we combined real-time ECG signal processing with a declarative JSON knowledge layer, a Rule-Based inference engine, and a Finite State Machine—achieving both algorithmic intelligence and strict aerospace predictability.
  • Parallel Multi-Crew Spacecraft Console: Instead of a conventional web login flow, we modeled an authentic spacecraft command dock where all 5 crew sessions run continuously in the background, complete with automated Extravehicular Activity (EVA GO / NO-GO) safety lockouts that counteract the astronaut "hero bias" of underreporting symptoms.
  • Active Verification & Just-in-Time Guidance: When pre-arrhythmic or VF patterns emerge, AEGIS does not merely flash an alarm—it takes over the workflow to guide the crew step-by-step through physical sensor confirmation, AED pad placement, defibrillation, and automated medkit inventory logging.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Communication Delays & Offline-First Resilience: Engineered specifically for Mars transit latencies (up to 44 minutes round-trip) and solar conjunction blackouts, maintaining local state persistence and an asynchronous Earth-sync telemetry queue.
  • Microgravity Physiological Adaptation: Calibrated normal baselines using NASA-STD-3001 rather than standard terrestrial ranges, accounting for cephalad fluid shifts and altered cardiovascular metrics in $0\text{g}$.
  • Human Factors & Skill Decay: Designed around the reality that astronauts are primarily pilots, engineers, and scientists who experience medical skill decay over multi-month missions, requiring intuitive visual body mapping and unambiguous step-by-step instructions.
  • Closed-Loop Environmental Interactions: Factored in spacecraft cabin variables ($\text{CO}_2$ partial pressure, $\text{O}_2$ levels, and radiation exposure) that directly influence arrhythmia risk.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Programming Languages & Data Formats: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3, and JSON (Declarative Clinical Knowledge, Variables, Rules, and FSM Transitions Schema).
  • Frontend & State Architecture: React, Vite, Zustand (with localStorage persistence for offline-first crew state management), Tailwind CSS, and Lucide-React.
  • Core Engines & Algorithms: Custom ECG Signal Processing & Feature Extraction module, Rule-Based Inference Engine, and Deterministic Finite State Machine (FSM).
    • NASA-STD-3001 (Vol. 2, Appendix E) for microgravity physiological and cabin environmental thresholds.
    • NASA ExMC Integrated Medical Model (IMM) & IMPACT 1.0 (119 Medical Conditions List / HRP-48036) for Ventricular Fibrillation clinical workflows and task impairment modeling.
    • NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) & LSDA Spaceflight Standard Measures for longitudinal baseline modeling.
    • PhysioNet MIT-BIH Malignant Ventricular Ectopy & Ventricular Fibrillation Parameters for ECG waveform signal validation.
